note: FNS 741.3 requires SNAP benefits to change in the same month as PA (Public Assistance) changes when the state has 30+ days advance knowledge, or no later than the following month with less notice. The OLG does not address this PA-change synchronization requirement anywhere. The Agency Error page (Cross Programs > Overpayments and Recovery > Agency Error) references 'failed to reduce the benefit level when the public assistance grant changed' as an example of agency error, confirming the obligation exists — but only in the context of error classification, not as worker-facing procedure or policy guidance. The OLG has general change processing timeliness rules (e.g., 106 CMR 366.120's 10-day/next-month rule for reported changes, referenced on the 'Add a New Person' page), but these are for household-reported changes, not PA mass changes initiated by the agency. There is no OLG content covering: (1) the specific timing requirement for synchronizing SNAP with PA grant changes, (2) procedures for processing PA mass changes affecting SNAP, or (3) the 30-day advance knowledge threshold that determines same-month vs. next-month processing. BEACON may handle PA-to-SNAP adjustments automatically for combo cases, but no OLG documentation confirms this.

Department Responsibility to Take Timely Action

_layer3.note: 106 CMR 366.130 explicitly requires that SNAP benefits be recomputed and effective in the same month as PA changes when the Department has 30+ days advance knowledge, or no later than the following month with less notice. This directly mirrors FNS 741.3 and is a binding state regulatory obligation. The CMR also requires notification per 366.130(D) and applies the same logic to federal benefit mass changes (SSA, SSI, VA). The OLG gap is a significant compliance gap: workers lack written procedure for handling PA mass changes, including the timing threshold, despite this being a state regulatory requirement.
